fixes.explanation: Close, but Jesus doesn't say that. He says, "So practice and observe everything they tell you." (Matthew 23:3) The seat of Moses, who led Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), is why their teaching still counts. Ignoring all of it would be tossing the whole batch because one cook was sloppy.

Yes, friend. Jesus says, "But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach." (Matthew 23:3) The words are fine to follow. The living is the part that doesn't match. That's like me teaching the recipe to everybody and never turning on my own oven.
That's it, baker. Jesus says they "…are not willing to lift a finger to move them." (Matthew 23:4) They tie up heavy loads and lay them on men's shoulders. Those heavy loads get no help from them.

You got it, baker. Jesus says, "All their deeds are done for men to see." (Matthew 23:5) Their deeds are done to be seen. I've stamped cookies for an audience before, but my mustache didn't need the applause.

True, baker! Jesus says they love "…the chief seats in the synagogues…" (Matthew 23:6) Those are the chief seats, the ones people notice. The verse also says they love the places of honor at banquets.
Not this time, friend. Jesus says they love "…the chief seats in the synagogues…" (Matthew 23:6) So the statement is true. The verse also says they love the places of honor at banquets.

Right, baker. Jesus says, "for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers." (Matthew 23:8) There are two reasons, and both are right there in the verse. Verse 10 has a matching line: "for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10)
That's right, baker. Jesus says, "…for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10) The Christ is the Messiah (John 1:41). Jesus names Him as the one Instructor.

Moses, who led Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), comes up in verse 2, so I see the pull. But Jesus says, "…for you have one Instructor, the Christ." (Matthew 23:10) Moses' seat is where the scribes and Pharisees sit. The one Instructor is the Christ.
That's what the scribes and Pharisees love, friend. They love "…the chief seats in the synagogues…" (Matthew 23:6) But Jesus says, "The greatest among you shall be your servant." (Matthew 23:11)
